title: Introducing Command Center
format_note: Silent-to-viewer text-and-UI film: claim cards on black alternate with white product screens; no speech, orchestral-string music bed, ends on a product-name lockup.
one_thing: Legal AI moves fast, you feel out of control, and Command Center lets you steer, benchmark against peers and act on it.

transcript.voice_style: No voice. Copy is carried by large serif cards and typed UI text.
transcript.script_shape: Problem in three typed cards (fast, new, out of control), then a claim, then three feature demos each introduced by a one-line black card, then a two-line payoff and lockup.

structure.frame0: Off-white ground; the headline 'Legal AI moves fast' types in letter by letter from t=0.017s and is complete by 0.4s (strips/window-01). The product is not yet on screen.
structure.first_3s: Claim line lands at 0.4s, then at 2.0s a left-aligned 'New models / New tools / New questions' list types while email notification cards stack in at top right (f0002, f0003).

Zoom into prompt box, query typed, send clicked, answer card 'Top power users' with five bars.

'Harvey / Command Center' lockup holds on black.

hero_moment.what: Generated M&A deck slide fills the side panel next to the finished chat answer (f0022, f0023), just after music section E starts at 40.5s.

ending.cta_text: none; product-name lockup 'Harvey Command Center' only
ending.what: Payoff lines on black, then a two-line lockup (serif Harvey over bold sans Command Center) static to the last frame (f0026 to f0028).

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Nine hard cuts, none inside a burst, longest shot 9.5s (37.1 to 46.6). Inside shots the pace comes from typing, list stacking, counters ticking and camera zooms, so something changes about every 1.5s (median hold 1.5s).

look.ground: Alternates near-white (0.679 of sampled frames) and pure black (0.321). Black carries claims; white carries product.
look.accent_use: Almost none: green +5% deltas and one italic word ('setting') at 48s. Colour is saved for the generated slide's teal.
look.type: Elegant serif for every claim and KPI number, clean grotesque for UI text, bold grotesque for 'Command Center'. Sentence case, centred on black cards, left-aligned beside UI.

title_measurements.text: See where you're leading or lagging

look.depth: Flat. Soft card shadows on UI, no parallax or 3D; the UI window has a faint drop shadow on the pale ground.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Hard zoom into a component until it fills the frame (prompt box f0009, Top power users card f0011, checklist f0016), then cut back to a full-window shot with the side panel.
product_ui.notes: Zoomed cards are readable (Top power users title ~34px high, f0011); full-dashboard shots (f0007, f0022) carry 8-12px labels that would not survive a phone. Fictional firm 'Whitford Lane' with consistent numbers (304/305 users).

motion.text_entry: Letter-by-letter typing with a per-letter fade, about 0.4s for 19 characters (strips/window-01, window-13). Lists type line by line; exits fade out top line first over about 0.4s (strips/window-04).
motion.ui_motion: KPI percentages count up while panels slide in (strips/window-07); chat answers type in; a slide image loads from grey placeholder to teal title slide in about 2s (f0021 to f0023).
motion.camera: Scale zooms into UI components and a slow push on the main window; no pans or whip moves seen.
motion.eases: Not measured by curve. Typing is linear and fast; fades on exit are quick and short; the dotted line and bars draw on at a steady rate (strips/window-14).

transitions.cause: A typed claim card completes and holds; the cut lands on a new screen or card.
Prompt submitted, answer types, slide appears in the side panel.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Claim cards hold 1.3-2.4s; the 0.5s + 0.3s per word rule needs 1.7-3.1s, so 'It's hard to feel like you're in control' (8 words, ~1.7s, rule 2.9s) and 'You're not just keeping up' fall short. Typing builds reading time in.

sound.music: Music only. audio.json describe tags: bowed_string_instrument 0.77, violin_fiddle 0.744, cello 0.671, orchestra 0.559; no steady beat (confidence 0.127). Five sections A-E at 0, 4, 17, 34.5 and 40.5s.
sound.sfx: Not identified; audio.json gives kind music and no sfx tag. Typing sounds, if any, were not verified.
sound.vo_music_balance: No voice. Music is the only layer; integrated -20.7 LUFS, true peak -3.5 dBTP, loudness range 10.2 LU.
sound.energy_arc: Quiet open (silence 0.08-0.395s), sections change at 4s, 17s, 34.5s and 40.5s; short-term max -17.2 LUFS. Section E runs 14.9s through the deck reveal and lockup.
sound.sync_to_picture: Not locked: cuts_on_strong_onset_share 0.222 against chance 0.192, a gap of 0.03. The one clear match is music section E starting at 40.5s just before the deck slide appears at about 42s.

good.observation: Claim cards on black alternate with product screens on white, so every cut changes ground as well as content and the story beat is readable without sound.
Zooming a single component to fill the frame makes small dashboard data legible and gives one focal point: the Top power users card is 68% of frame width.
Typed text is used for both claims and the user's prompt, so the film teaches 'type a question, get an answer' with the same motion as its headlines.
Data stays consistent across shots (304 to 305 users, +5%, Whitford Lane, Top power users names) so the UI reads as one real product.
The hard, flat cut on a completed card feels intentional because each cut follows a finished typed line; no effects needed.
The ending holds a bare two-line lockup for over five seconds, about a tenth of the film, which gives the product name time to register.
good.evidence: f0026 to f0028; longest static run to 54s

weak.observation: Several claim cards are shorter than the reading rule: 'It's hard to feel like you're in control' holds ~1.7s for 8 words, and 'You're not just keeping up' ~1.3s.
Full-window dashboard shots rely on 8-12px labels and a 22-word suggestion paragraph; none would read on a phone without the zooms.
The Harvey Command Center flash at 7.15s is visible only for a fraction of a second before the next claim types in, so the first name reveal is easy to miss.
Loudness is -20.7 LUFS integrated, six LU under a social master, and the cuts do not follow the music.

rule_candidates.rule: Use a typed claim line as the hook: start the headline typing at frame 0 and finish it within 0.5s (19 characters in 0.4s); the product can wait until after 2s.
rule_candidates.evidence: strips/window-01-0.017s.jpg; f0001 headline only, product first at 2.0s

rule_candidates.rule: Put statements on black and product screens on near-white, and cut between them; about a third of runtime on black (0.321) made each change of beat obvious.
A film with a median shot of 4.5s and nine hard cuts (9.74 cuts per minute, no burst) can still read as energetic if motion inside each shot (typing, counters, draw-on lines) changes every ~1.5s.
rule_candidates.evidence: metrics.json rhythm median_shot_s 4.52, bursts []; events median_hold_s 1.5

rule_candidates.rule: Hard cuts are fine as the main seam when each follows a completed typed line and alternates ground colour; all nine seams here were hard cuts.
Count numbers up while a dashboard assembles (39% to 56% in about 0.7s) so the first full UI shot shows the product working, not a static screenshot.
Zoom a UI component to at least 60% of frame width (Top power users card ~68%) for the data beat, then step back to the full window for context.
rule_candidates.evidence: f0011 card spans about 870 of 1280px; f0007 full window

rule_candidates.rule: Hold the closing name lockup for at least 5s (about 10% of runtime) with no CTA text; the lockup titles measure 8.3-10.3% of frame height.
Master quieter than -14 LUFS is a weakness: this film sits at -20.7 LUFS integrated with a -3.5 dBTP peak, leaving 6.7 LU of headroom.
